DownloadMetrics.description: Download documents: [`CommonMetrics`] plus how much the wire bytes expanded on disk.

client_version.description: Version of the `hf-xet` client that produced this document.

cpu_count.description: Parallelism available to the client process. 0 when it could not be determined.

direction.description: Which half of the transfer this describes: `upload` or `download`.

dry_run.description:
Whether this was a dry run, which performs no real uploads. Always false in practice, since
dry runs do not report at all; present so the field is never ambiguous.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock time from session construction to this document being built, in milliseconds.

endpoint_host.description:
Host component of the CAS endpoint. Never a full URL - a path or query could carry
something sensitive.

error_class.description:
Coarse failure bucket: `none` when nothing went wrong, otherwise `auth`, `network`,
`timeout`, `rate_limited`, `server_error`, `not_found`, `io`, `format`, `cancelled`,
`internal`, or `other`. Deliberately coarse - error text could contain file paths.

ewma_throughput_bps.description:
The client's own EWMA estimate, for comparison against the wall-clock figures. Zero rather
than absent when the sampler never had enough observations.

expansion_ratio.description:
Logical bytes produced per wire byte - dedup and compression combined, from the
downloader's side.

logical_throughput_bps.description:
Logical throughput over the whole transfer: `total_bytes_completed` per second. Exceeds
`throughput_bps` by the dedup and compression factor.

n_files.description: Number of files in the transfer.

os.description:
Operating system the client is running on, as reported by the Rust target
(`linux`, `macos`, `windows`, ...).

outcome.description:
How the transfer ended: `ok`, `error`, `cancelled`, `aborted`, `dropped`, or
`in_progress` for a heartbeat.

peak_concurrency.description: Highest number of concurrent connections the adaptive-concurrency controller reached.

schema_version.description:
Version of this metric vocabulary. Incremented when keys are added, so a query can tell an
absent key from an older client that never emitted it.

seq.description: 0 for the first document; increments per heartbeat.

terminal.description:
Exactly one document per `transfer_id` carries `true`. Filter on it to get one row per
transfer without any group-by.

throughput_bps.description:
Wire throughput over the whole transfer: `transfer_bytes_completed` per second, computed
from `duration_ms`. Deterministic, unlike the EWMA below.

total_bytes.description: Logical bytes, before dedup and compression.

total_bytes_completed.description: Logical bytes actually finished. Below `total_bytes` for a failed or abandoned transfer.

transfer_bytes.description: Bytes actually moved over the wire.

transfer_id.description:
Unique per transfer. A single `XetSession` id can cover both an upload commit and a
download group, so `session_id` alone does not identify a transfer.

UploadMetrics.description: Upload documents: [`CommonMetrics`] plus dedup effectiveness and shard finalization.

client_version.description: Version of the `hf-xet` client that produced this document.

compression_ratio.description:
Compressed xorb bytes over the new bytes that produced them: below 1.0 means compression
helped. 0.0 when nothing new was uploaded.

cpu_count.description: Parallelism available to the client process. 0 when it could not be determined.

dedup_bytes.description: Logical bytes that did not need uploading because an identical chunk already existed.

dedup_chunks.description: Chunks that already existed and were not uploaded.

dedup_ratio.description:
Share of logical bytes avoided by dedup: `dedup_bytes / total_bytes`. 0.0 when there was
nothing to transfer.

defrag_prevented_dedup_bytes.description:
Bytes that could have been deduplicated but were re-uploaded anyway, because doing
otherwise would have fragmented the xorb past the defrag threshold. The cost of the
fragmentation-vs-dedup tradeoff.

defrag_prevented_dedup_chunks.description: Chunks re-uploaded despite being deduplicable, for the defrag reason above.

direction.description: Which half of the transfer this describes: `upload` or `download`.

dry_run.description:
Whether this was a dry run, which performs no real uploads. Always false in practice, since
dry runs do not report at all; present so the field is never ambiguous.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock time from session construction to this document being built, in milliseconds.

endpoint_host.description:
Host component of the CAS endpoint. Never a full URL - a path or query could carry
something sensitive.

error_class.description:
Coarse failure bucket: `none` when nothing went wrong, otherwise `auth`, `network`,
`timeout`, `rate_limited`, `server_error`, `not_found`, `io`, `format`, `cancelled`,
`internal`, or `other`. Deliberately coarse - error text could contain file paths.

ewma_throughput_bps.description:
The client's own EWMA estimate, for comparison against the wall-clock figures. Zero rather
than absent when the sampler never had enough observations.

finalize_ms.description:
Shard consolidation, upload, and registration, in milliseconds. 0 for a transfer that
never reached finalization.

global_dedup_bytes.description:
Subset of `dedup_bytes` deduplicated against the global index rather than local state.
The rest was matched within this session or from the local shard cache.

global_dedup_chunks.description: Subset of `dedup_chunks` matched against the global index.

ingest_ms.description:
Chunking, hashing, and xorb upload: session start until `finalize` was called, in
milliseconds. 0 on a heartbeat, where the phase has not ended.

logical_throughput_bps.description:
Logical throughput over the whole transfer: `total_bytes_completed` per second. Exceeds
`throughput_bps` by the dedup and compression factor.

n_files.description: Number of files in the transfer.

new_bytes.description: Logical bytes that were new and had to be uploaded.

new_chunks.description: Chunks that were new and had to be uploaded.

os.description:
Operating system the client is running on, as reported by the Rust target
(`linux`, `macos`, `windows`, ...).

outcome.description:
How the transfer ended: `ok`, `error`, `cancelled`, `aborted`, `dropped`, or
`in_progress` for a heartbeat.

peak_concurrency.description: Highest number of concurrent connections the adaptive-concurrency controller reached.

schema_version.description:
Version of this metric vocabulary. Incremented when keys are added, so a query can tell an
absent key from an older client that never emitted it.

seq.description: 0 for the first document; increments per heartbeat.

shard_bytes_uploaded.description: Shard (metadata) bytes sent to CAS during finalization.

shard_validation_entries.description:
File entries the server verified while registering the shards. A proxy for how much work
finalization asked of the server.

shards_completed.description:
Shards the server confirmed as fully registered. Below `shards_total` when finalization
did not complete.

terminal.description:
Exactly one document per `transfer_id` carries `true`. Filter on it to get one row per
transfer without any group-by.

throughput_bps.description:
Wire throughput over the whole transfer: `transfer_bytes_completed` per second, computed
from `duration_ms`. Deterministic, unlike the EWMA below.

total_bytes.description: Logical bytes, before dedup and compression.

total_bytes_completed.description: Logical bytes actually finished. Below `total_bytes` for a failed or abandoned transfer.

total_chunks.description: Chunks the content-defined chunker produced across all files.

transfer_bytes.description: Bytes actually moved over the wire.

transfer_id.description:
Unique per transfer. A single `XetSession` id can cover both an upload commit and a
download group, so `session_id` alone does not identify a transfer.

xorb_bytes_uploaded.description:
Compressed xorb bytes sent to CAS. This plus `shard_bytes_uploaded` is the real upload
cost of the transfer.

description:
The `metrics` object of a POST /v1/telemetry document, one shape per transfer direction. This file is the source of truth for the metric vocabulary: every property carries a description of what it measures and its unit.

Generated from xet_data/src/telemetry/payload.rs - edit the Rust structs, not this file, and regenerate with `UPDATE_TELEMETRY_SCHEMA=1 cargo test -p xet-data --lib telemetry::schema`.

Compatibility: adding a property is backward compatible. Removing one, or changing its type, is NOT - consumers typically assign a column or field type on first sight and cannot change it in place afterwards. If a metric's meaning or unit changes, add a new property rather than repurposing the existing one (`duration_us` alongside `duration_ms`, not `duration_ms` becoming a float). CI enforces this.

Every value is a scalar - never null, never nested, never an array. Integers fit in an unsigned 64-bit integer; numbers are finite doubles. No file names, paths, hashes, repository ids, or user ids appear anywhere in this vocabulary.
title: Xet client transfer telemetry metrics
